source_en:
Halvern Room, half past the Tenth Bell. Knock twice, then once. Five of them — Devereaux, Halhurst, Old Pellaby, Tannig, Anderson.

Be brief. Be brief. Be brief.

Open with the joke about Halhurst's clocks. Clocks paid by the hour. Wait for the laugh. If they do not laugh, turn serious abruptly.

Then: the Church is exhausted... Sold its last seat three hundred years ago... No new pews... Nothing it could offer me would be enough even if it still had something to offer.

Then: Mr. Moore is the only ledger in the city large enough to carry what is coming. Not flattery. "This is merely Mathematics."

Then: buy in now, or be bought later. The wise man does not need this said twice. (say this out loud so they think of themselves wise)

The Veil... PAUSE HERE... The Veil is a wall between two rooms. One side has stopped paying its rent. The other side has been keeping the books for a thousand years. The rent is owed. The reopening is not a question. It is a date.

Tell them: my name is on the contract.

Tell them: I am not selling. I am inviting.

On Halhurst's daughter — only speak of her if he raises her name first. Then: She is well thought of by Master Felwyl. Let it sit.

Close. Slowly. We are not buyers. We are founders. We are the seed of the next House.

Smile. They will think it modesty.
— B. C.

source_en: A note from one physician to another.

Forgive me. I hope you live to see this, but I could not wait. 

If you are reading this, brother, do not go home. The inquisition has both our names, though from whom I couldn't guess.  It might have been anyone, but it doesn't matter now. Anynmore than the truth matters.  

So go West. Follow the river out, and head for the woods. Rember that place where grandfather took us hunting as children?  

You got your first rabbit there, if I remember. A better shot than me, even then.

I pray I will see you again. If not in this life, then in the hereafter. 

If I don’t make it, and you do, then know this about my last moments. I will try to take one of the bastards with me.  

-Your brother

source_en:
Shipments from the herbary have ceased completely now, so I’ve not been able to properly mix my tinctures. 

I’ve had to dilute what supplies I have down to the point of imagination.  It’s just as well then that so much of the city has fled. 

I had only one patient come in yesterday for her weekly powders. Usually, it's half-ash, half-desiccated bone broth that's prescribed for a touch of the dropsy, but now it's ash alone I have to serve. 

Whether her constitution can tell the difference, I don't suppose I'm like to ever know.  

Today, no one has come in at all.

It’s only the brave who stayed. And the foolish.  

Since my own tincture for bravery—good mead—has long run out, I guess I know which I am. 

I’ve nothing to share now but wishes and water. 

But then, maybe that’s all I ever had.

Gildenarch deserves what’s coming for it.

source_en: Transcribed from the wall of St. Enoch.

What's reborn can be rekilled. Remember that, you fools. 

It's the cult that brought this down on all of us. I'd wager anything.

It was only me that ran. 

It’s important I write that here, so it’s recorded. I’d want no stench of desertion to be levied against the others, who fought bravely to a man. 

Their names should be clean, unlike mine—Daerun Bogmire, as it’s recorded in the sentry lists. A name, even bad as it is, that I couldn't live up to. 

Or maybe I did live up to it.  To run is in my name.

What does heaven look like, I wonder? Or mayhap it’s hell I should be thinking on. 

Soon I’ll know. The cut is deep, but that’s not what I’m afraid of. It’s the bite. The bite worries me. This bite that gives me frenzied thoughts. 

It’s not too long now afore I go. I feel it rising, like a fever. Please forgive me.     

I seen the walking bones. I knew them when they held flesh. Good men, some of them. Bad men, others. But as bones they are made equal as never they were in life. They are the damned. As soon am I.  

Or am already. 

Goodbye. 

The Bogmire name dies with me.  Good riddance.

source_en:
Another test subject was martyred today in pursuit of knowledge. We managed to keep his soul bound to flesh for nearly a fortnight after his heart stopped beating. 

Just before he expired the second time, he looked up at me and spoke my mother’s name. 

He could not possibly have known it, of course. 

At least not before he died the first time. 

He told me that my mother knew what I’d done. That she’d whispered to him that she was ashamed. 

I told him my mother had been dead these many years, and asked where he'd heard the whispers.  

He only smiled and said, "Not in Divine's Throne Room, that's for certain."

source_en: One I wish I could forget

Your Eminence, I pray we are not too late. I don’t understand the church’s slow response to this threat. The Cult of the Reborn grows and grows, like a noxious and dangerous weed in the beautiful garden of our city, yet we do nothing!

They call us toothless old fools as they incite heresy in the street. 

Why does the church not react? The influence of this cult increases by the day. There have been murders, kidnappings, and even rumors of heretical experimentations. Stories of abominations have reached my ears.  

There is a sickness spreading through the world, and this cult is at the heart of it.

The enemy is not just at our doorstep, but also seated at our very tables. The Lunitarian Church must take action before the wound grows too great. Please, I implore you.  

Ever your faithful servant,

-Father Ortney

"All? Even the accuser?"

"They will all confess to something."

The time has come, Mathias. We have belayed our response long enough. The disorder and chaos that we’ve allowed to fester within the city has now justified extreme action.  

In fact, the people hunger for it. They yearn for the strength of the iron hand. 

Even the worst heresy, sometimes, is an act in service to the greater good.  And make no mistake, there is no greater good without evil.  No advancement without destruction. No immortality without death.  

The death of others, at least.

As prefect of the Doctrine, you've done your part, your Emminence. Now we will do ours.

The people have asked for the touch of the iron hand.

Now, Mathias, we will give them what they want. 

-Solomon.

I heard the children singing in the courtyard today. A new rhyme lilting from their innocent little voices.  

At first I didn't understand what they were saying, but when I did, I brought them in and put them to work on their numbers, forbidding them to speak for the rest of the day.  

I copied down the rhyme here before I forgot, in case it's needed for evidence.  

The rhyme goes-

"Where the red rash spreads, comes the never dead. 
Where pain flees, sunlight never sees. 
Where old age goes, the devil knows. The devil knows. The devil knows."

And then there was a second part, which would surely be some form of heresy if the inquisitors ever heard it.

"To the church goes the tithes 
To the kingdom the taxes
To Hell goes the souls 
Who touch the Abraxas."

source_en: From the papers of the High Tutor

This one claimed to know nothing even after we broke his hands. We asked after his brother, but he would not give him up. Then we started on his feet. Then his tongue.  

Eventually, we broke him. Or thought we had. 

He feigned cooperation, and because he could no longer speak, motioned for a quill and parchment to be put in his hands for a signed confession.  

We gave him a quill, but the moment the inks were put before him, he smiled bloodily and dashed the ink in the guard's eyes. 

He managed to kill one of the inquisitors before he was put down. An ugly business. 

His brother has yet to be found.

source_en: Final Entry of a Soldier's Journal

Before the Lunitarian Church established the Crimson Concordat, attempts to reduce instances of Nephilim going feral were met with little success. Though some Nephilim made noble attempts at integration into civilian life, all it took was one to become possessed by their Angel to wreak havoc.

Demands to protect the common folk began to outpace ethical considerations given the trials posed by the Greaet Reconstruction.

1.	The Cessation of Old Ways
  a.	Velchorians will hereby reject the fallen gods who lost the cosmic war which befel our realm. The Velchorian Empire hereby recognizes Lunarin as the heir to the Cosmic Throne.
  b.	All former faiths will hereby be known as paganus. Gods of the Earth, and Archetypes of the Soul shall henceforth be rejected and are illegal within the Imperial realm. So that man might follow in Lunarin’s Holy Moonlight.

source_en:
Gallant,
Your prose... beautiful as ever. 
But once again, all that comes of it are lies. Youth believes love can conquer all. But the books tell me otherwise. 
I waited under the willow. I watched the stars twinkle and fade. Fire to coal, my heart moved with them—as I realized, you were not coming. 
I cursed you. I even threw a book! Can you imagine? Of course I quickly dusted it off and set it back atop the shelf – what has The Traveling Tales of Tiverna ever done to me? 
But all of that was before I got the news. 
It’s worse than I feared. It’s not that you forgot me for one night. It’s that you’re gone forever, a fading star out of reach. 
I have no idea where you are, but your Officer says this will reach you. Of course I don’t believe him, but writing is a healing of its own.
Goodbye my love. 
We were young once.
Watching branches glitter the stars
But youth leaves us now 
As we leave each other naught but scars.

Your faded star,
Mereda

How could the knight who killed Valahk Nor, Gallant the Wise, The Honest, The Kind, Gallant the Brave be executed by the same Church he saved? 
Today is the day the Church took my faded star in their palm and blotted it from the sky.
Gone, gone, gone forever more.
Oh Gallant, if ever I held on to a fleck of youth, a fleck of hope, I drop it now and fold it into this letter for you. The last part of me that I saved, I give freely now, in this final letter. This farewell to your tomb.
Of course I’ll remember. 
Even if easier to forget. 
I shall never forgive the Church for this day.
I renounce and study at Elk Grove Academy.

May every book bring memories of you
As you rest ever after in your tomb
--Mereda

 لذا سأنقذ هذه الأرواح الضائعة؛ سأمنحهم الفرصة، والاجتهاد، والأمل. وأخيرًا، والأهم من ذلك، شيئًا ليكرهوه. بعضهم البعض.

source_en:
Solomon, your absence at the gathering has aroused suspicion among the Patriarchs and Matriarchs of the other clans. I do not know what it is you’re doing in Velchoria, but I must remind you of the Pact. Cain is dead, and it is better he remains that way; we’ve no desire to go to war against the Church or all of Eden, for that matter. Without mankind, we have no cattle, and as long as Cain can’t reach us, we are free to use his blood as we see fit. We have something good going on; other clans do not want you jeopardizing it for your religious nonsense.

Lastly, I’d be remiss not to remind you that you still owe Clan Telvaught our blade Scirax. If you do not return it to us, we may come to collect it.

source_en: It appears the Lunitarian’s occupation of Gildenarch was far more interesting than I could have imagined. Their interest in the Abraxas Stones was no mere fall from grace; they were direct orders from the Holy Lineage themselves over 400 years ago. The irony that I was far more devout than my superiors at that time doesn’t surprise me. The slave morality they’ve instilled in their subordinates kept us from ambition, yet the Holy Lineage themselves have greater ambitions than perhaps even I, today. Residents credit Solomon Moore, the celebrity entrepreneur from Nachtendale for his efforts in reviving Gildenarch’s mines in the Mystic Peaks mountains west of the city. The reopened mines utilize Nachtstahl’s proprietary steel to build reinforced shafts and maintenance tunnels.

Clan Telvaught:

Guild of Academics and Archaeologists. Led by Professor Peter Garrus Telvaught in efforts to uncover lost artifacts from the ancient era of The Coil. First to abandon Cain’s Covenant, first to die.


Clan Sirius: 

Founded by Matron Delilah Hexxus Sirus. Traitor to Cain, abandoned his crusade and started a guild of petty cutthroats and informants.

Clan Inari:

Founded by Aaron Chester Inari. Occultist and owner of Inari Weaponry. The Clan have become isolationists, interfacing with Eden solely through market competition providing arms and armaments to various Armaean Kingdoms. 

Clan Harington:

Also called The Pale Rose. Founded by Madam Margarette Harrington the owner of the Harrington House. An academy of wizards and sorcerers in eastern Norundiir far beyond the reach of the Lunitarian Church.

source_en:
An unorthodox exploration of Lunitarian myth and legend that scrutinizes the conventional narrative of Archangel Maedrael. A particular passage sticks out to you.

It could not be understated just how unlike men the High Daemons of Ludereon are. They are not corporeal beings but instead constructed of a sort of “Resonant Energy”. If records from the old world are to be believed, they’ve taken many forms, in fact.

 According to canon, the invention of Angelic Sigils, the magick used to give an Angel a particular form with attributes, comes directly from the Archangel himself—a puzzling detail if only canon is taken into account. If we consider my prior explorations, there may be more to Maedrael than we’ve come to believe. I propose a theory, one perhaps well outside of the realm of accepted thought, that Maedrael is not of Ludereon. How else can one possess the 'self directed will' akin to that of man?

My Mereda, with a heart that feels set aflame by Cain himself, I burn for your touch. My ears can hear nothing but your cooing laugh that flows past your lips like a joke only you will ever know. 
My angel tells me I am being foolish – of course I am. He tells me I should focus on my training. Why would I give even a fraction of my thought on that punishing, brutal, and cruel treatment, when I can close my eyes and see your form laid bare before me.
I have not been lucky in my young life, but finally winning you over to my passions and pulling you away from your books is my greatest fortune. You said we were doomed from the start, but I don’t care. I would fight through the infernal gates and slay a thousand souls to once again feel your body against mine. You may think we are doomed, but from the lingering taste of you upon my lips I know you don’t care either. 
The world, no, all of the heavens and hells are at war, my love. Tomorrow is a promise neither of us can keep. But tonight, my dearest, tonight I can promise that if you meet me under our old willow tree I will burn the heavens themselves with my passion for you. My hands have no purpose if not to hold you. My heart has no reason to beat if not near you --
My commander enters, I must go. Be with me tonight.
I am forever truly yours

My Mereda,
I have no reason to believe this will find you. If I have learned one thing since they pulled me out of training it is that war, real war, is chaos. I have no doubt that it was created by the Infernal Legion. No rules, no order, just violence, blood, and the howls of the dying. 
I have seen men fall to their knees and beg for their mothers. I have watched thousands of men be cut down in front me. The crimson mist of their blood fills the air. I can still taste their blood on my tongue. 
This is all because of one demon. Valahk-Nor. They call him a general, but what even is that to the Infernal Legions? He’s just a bigger more deadly demon than the rest. I care not. I’m going to kill this demon spawn for taking me away from you. If it weren’t for him, I would have had that night with you under the willow. 
I am going to run my sword through Valahk-Nor's throat for you. I will drag his head back from this unholy place and present it to you as my amends for leaving. And then, I will take you in my arms and we will make up for the days and months we have lost, Mereda. My passion has only grown since I have been pulled away from you. It is all consuming for me. 
I  am off, the troops are marshalling. I know I said that tomorrow was a promise neither one of us could give, but I promise you, I will return and we will have our time under the willow.
I am forever truly yours,

Once more, I am roused from my sleep by gut-wrenching nightmares. The frequency is now unbearable, and I can no longer sustain my life this way.

Again I find  myself in the graveyard behind St. Uriel’s chapel, under that same accursed crimson moonlight basking the yard in an ethereal haze.

There, cloaked men gathered around that rotten, gnarled tree, whispering profane and terrible things before a woman chained to its trunk. Suddenly, I am taken behind her eyes, and I witness the men brandish a knife.

I am spared witness to the bloodshed, but I cannot help but feel it's true.

Lunarin is the Dragon! The Demiurge lives once more through the Church. A Millenia of Lies befell man after the Imperial Conversion. 

I have good news, brothers and sisters. Though our forefathers were deceived by the Lunitarians, there yet remains another way to freedom! Freedom from this earth, from suffering and pain, just as we were before the Demiurge ensared our souls in the Coil! The Initiated know the truth about Lost Akyreon, the realm of Aeons Given Flesh, who’ve been scorned by Archons of the Throne. Their unjust persecution is the fate of man should we continue to unwittingly serve the Dragon. 

The Church calls them Demons; we shall call them Shepherds! The Shepherds have given us a gift. 

Tonight we must accept their offering and partake in the powers of the realm beyond this accursed veil.

source_en: Forgive my hesitancy towards Felwyl’s spiritual claims; he was always an odd one. His interest in the occult, though not inherently a problem itself, does concern me. I knew a practitioner once, a woman named Mereda. She was an alumna of Elk Grove back in the day, and she, too, was a magician. A lovely woman whom I’d trust dearly, but I’ll always remember what she told me: “never trust a demon”. I know damn well what Felwyl’s been up to, and I’m sure that Solomon figure has something to do with it. The Flora Felwyl has been presenting to his students is not of this world; he’s obtained it from some unholy means, and I’d rather not be involved with it. I have a strange paralysis. Like I don’t know where to start. 
It tingles really as it takes control. The red veins outlining the pace of my heart, the quickening of my pulse. 
My master calls to me.
From the other side. 
Where he awaits a door.
The door is ours door to build. The door is my task.
Under the guidance of Lord Felwyl we shall build
a door of many hands, intertwined, all outstretched together in welcoming. 
Hands of the working folk. Hands of the non-believers. Hands of the unwilling.
One taste of the bloom and they move together, molding and forming into one, bodies becoming a single, purified organism, and their hands reach, reaching, stretching and ripping and breaking together in unison, to welcome your second coming, my Lord. 
Together as one.
They reach from the red bloom.
Yes. That’s it. 
I know exactly where to start. 
Thank you master. 
You shall have your door soon.

Lord Felwyl,
Sincerest apologies my Lord, as I know you are very busy. Very busy, indeed. But I write to bring to your attention matters at Ramshorn Keep.
We, your humble servants, and in your own words, chosen ones, The Reborn, are being woefully mistreated by these… new arrivals. 
Ever since we opened the gate to the other side and welcomed them in, they’ve been regretfully barbaric.
No language. No manners. They’ve even killed some of our brothers.
My Lord, I do not believe they even share our cause of a fully unified soul. A united Red Bloom.
I know that a patrician such as yourself would never stand for this. If only you knew. 
So I have written merely to bring this matter to your attention.
Your Servant,
Calum

Nothing comes without its price

Charles

The dark was the kindest thing that ever happened to me.

I am being chosen. I have never been chosen for anything before.

Eleven years. New owners. They forgot me. The slot opens but no face comes. Food still arrives. I do not ask.

Nineteen years. I hear the keep eat itself. Screams that aren't screams. Singing in the wrong throats. A great wet thing dragged past my door and licked the slot. I licked back.

The man in the wall is my friend now. He says when they come for me I should knock three times. He says he'll let me in.

source_en:
Solomon — 

You ask if I have the stomach. I have eaten venison while a poacher hung dripping from my rafters, keeping time with the strings. I do not lack stomach. 

The keep is yours. Take it down to the sea-stones if it pleases you. The lower wards too — I'm told the air there is rich, and that the men who survive long enough develop a most remarkable patience. 

You offer me red, and long red years to drink it. I accept. I would have signed for the offer alone, without the keep — but you are a man of style, and I shall not deprive you of the pleasure of payment. 

I'll be at the Aemar after the second course. Have something young ready. The first hunger, I'm told, is a memorable thing. 

— H. Caldwell
